text: Donetsk. I spent the whole trip thinking up something to say when those rooftops came into view. Now I haven’t got a word. Even the dragon’s gone quiet.
A woman from Donetsk wrote to me. She’s moved three times over the years, and she still carries her old house key. Every morning before she goes out, she pats that pocket to make sure it’s there.
I’d like to hear that key turn in the lock. For now there are enemy aircraft over the city. What do you need to know, Bondarenko?
All three aircraft types up there?
All three. An even hundred this time, so pace yourself all the way to the last one. And call in when you land. I’ve got used to hearing your partner breathing into the microphone.
